name: intraday_poc-train
notes: The PRODUCTION fit, TUNED: one LSTM per symbol, its hidden width chosen by a grid search scored on an embargoed tail the fit never sees. Run from the child root after the backfill is published: python -m dskit.pipeline run configs/run-train.json --asof 2026-08-28 --adapter intraday_poc. Then point the forward loop at the run dir: python -m intraday_poc.live --run-dir <run dir> --source-config configs/source-backfill.json --artifact AAPL=artifacts/qhat__aapl --artifact MSFT=artifacts/qhat__msft. The --artifact pair is REQUIRED here and is the loop's own documented hatch: the trainers are foreach instances, so their node keys carry the fan-out's double underscore (qhat__aapl) while the loop's default convention is artifacts/qhat_<symbol> — the hatch exists precisely so a document may rename its nodes without an edit to live.py. Everything else the loop still READS out of the run dir (config.json) — price field, gap bound, declared module class — so none of it is restated there. What changed from the untuned document, and why to accept it: the fit now stops at splits.train_end_ms instead of consuming every published bar, because a search whose objective scores rows its trials trained on grades memorization, and the biggest grid value always wins. The shipped artifact is therefore blind to the selection tail; refit after moving the cuts forward when that matters more than the tuning does.

foreach.notes: The symbol universe, and the reason this document has a fan-out at all: the search's space key names the TEMPLATE (qhat.module_params.hidden_size) and the expansion re-aims it at every instance, so ONE declaration searches every symbol over ONE grid. Written longhand the same search needs a space key per symbol — copies with nothing pinning them, so editing one and forgetting the other searches the two symbols over different grids and calls the difference a result. Add a third symbol by adding a key here and to source-backfill.json's universe, and nothing else. Keys are the RAW vendor symbols because $each substitutes them whole into the filters; node keys take their lowercase slug (qhat -> qhat__aapl). What the fan-out does NOT do: tie the two symbols to one tuned VALUE. Two instances are two independent overrides and hpo-grid crosses them, so three widths over two symbols is nine trials and the winner may pair 16 with 64 — see the search node's notes.

rows.notes: One model per symbol — the PoC's design, so each series is fit on its own dynamics — over the window [2026-01-01, train_end_ms]. The band between train_end_ms and val_start_ms belongs to NO split: a next-bar label resolves in one minute, so the embargo is discipline made visible rather than a horizon the label needs. WHY the history starts in 2026 rather than at the store's 2021 open, and what to change to widen it: the engine evaluates a fit's final training loss in ONE unbatched forward pass (dskit.pipeline.libs.torch, TorchTrain._final_loss), so peak memory is O(rows x lookback x hidden_size) — 940k AAPL windows at hidden_size 64 asks for 24.3 GB and dies on a 17 GB box, measured, at trial 3 of the grid. The start bound is a MEMORY ceiling wearing a modelling choice's clothes and should be deleted the day that pass is batched; until then it is declared here where it can be seen, once, for both symbols. It is a literal because there is no train_start_ms in the splits grammar — the cuts carve the future, not the horizon.

val_rows.notes: The selection window: the rows the search's objective is measured on, and the ONLY rows in this document no trial ever fits. They are wired to the forecast node, never to the trainer — see qhat's notes for why no monitor is declared.

qhat.notes: ADR-0025 declared seam: the document names the child's nn.Module and the optimizer; the module owns the flat-lag-vector -> LSTM-sequence resequencing, so the pack's default RowVectorAdapter carries it. features MUST stay ret_lag_0..ret_lag_{lookback-1} in order and module_params.lookback must equal the window node's lookback — the module refuses a width mismatch at run. hidden_size 32 is the DECLARED baseline the search overrides per trial; leaving it at the middle of the grid keeps the untuned document runnable and keeps this fit's params identical to run-backtest.json's (pinned by test_configs.py). device: cpu makes the compute target visible (the engine's default is already CPU; device is declared, never detected). optimizer_params names Adam's other knobs at their library defaults so they are visible and tunable, not a silent zero. NO monitor, deliberately, even though val_rows now exist in this document: monitoring would select the epoch on the very rows the search's objective scores, so one set would pick both the checkpoint and the architecture — the optimism run-backtest.json's notes warn about. val_rows stay unwired here and the last epoch's weights ship, exactly as before.

fc.notes: One belief per selection-window minute — the trainer's signal predicts straight off the fitted module; a row without full feature coverage is skipped, never fabricated. Downstream of the searched trainer, so every trial re-runs it.

bars.notes: Role data: the onboarding store's deduplicated bar records, bitemporally resolved (latest acquired_at wins per (symbol, ts)). root is relative to the invoking cwd — run from the child root. Shared: read once, filtered per symbol, and untouched by every trial.

window.notes: 30 one-minute log returns per row, next-bar return as label. max_gap_minutes 5 tolerates thin IEX minutes without ever bridging a session boundary; windows crossing a larger gap are dropped, not interpolated. Shared and clean, so the search re-executes only the trainers and what they feed — never this scan.

params.provenance_waiver: rows already carry their symbol; the ports are split by symbol upstream, so a port tag would duplicate the field

forecasts.notes: Port fan-out is OPT-IN: the port written 'forecasts__each' becomes one port per foreach key (forecasts__aapl, forecasts__msft), so adding a symbol never edits this node. Both symbols' beliefs in one stream for the selector; key=symbol proves the ports stayed disjoint.

params.provenance_waiver: rows already carry their symbol; the ports are split by symbol upstream, so a port tag would duplicate the field

labeled.notes: The selection window's rows with their y_next labels — what realizes each pick after the fact. Not downstream of the trainers, so a trial never re-runs it.

select.notes: The search's OBJECTIVE node: at each minute pick exactly one symbol, maximizing predicted next-bar return; metrics.total_realized is the summed realized log return of those picks. The same program run-backtest.json scores its folds with, and the same one live.py runs a minute at a time — so the architecture chosen here is chosen by the number the PoC actually cares about, not by a proxy loss. split: val says which rows it reads, and the engine refuses an objective that reads anything else.

search.notes: The capstone, kept deliberately small: ONE categorical knob over three widths, so the first tracked experiment tests the plumbing rather than a hypothesis. select: max because total_realized is a return — minimizing it would ship the architecture that lost the most, and hpo-grid's default is min. The space key names the foreach TEMPLATE and expands to one override per symbol; the search is therefore JOINT over the pair — 3 widths x 2 symbols = 9 trials, each refitting both models — and its winner may pair different widths, which is a result to read rather than a value this document adopts. No n_trials: nine trials IS the whole grid, and subsampling something this small trades a complete comparison for a rank seed. No seeds ensemble: it multiplies an already real cost, and the trainers' loader.seed pins every fit, so a re-run reproduces the winner exactly. The driver re-executes only the dirty subgraph per trial — the trainers, fc, forecasts, select — never the store scan or the windows, then re-applies the winner once so everything downstream reads the tuned pass. The winner is REPORTED, never written back: promoting it means moving hidden_size in this document AND in run-backtest.json together (test_configs.py pins the two fits identical), and an asymmetric winner must additionally defeat test_the_symbol_twins_share_a_regime — the argument promotion should have to win.

splits.notes: Causal cuts as epoch-ms, the only split kind a minute-bar document may declare: 2026-08-06 ends the fit, a one-day embargo band follows, 2026-08-07..2026-08-29 is the selection window the search scores, and the test band to 2026-09-05 is declared and deliberately UNREAD — nothing in this document may consume it, and it is where an honest out-of-sample check goes when one is built. Move all four forward together as the store grows; they are what decides how much history the shipped artifact saw.

sinks.notes: A LOCAL sqlite store beside the run root — no server to start, nothing to reach over a network, and the pack proves the file writable at plan time rather than swallowing the failure at run time. Spelled as a class reference so no registration call is needed anywhere in the child's code. The path is relative to the invoking cwd, the same discipline as bars.root. What lands here: one entry per RUN, carrying every node's declared params flattened to the override spelling (search.space, qhat__aapl.module_params.hidden_size, ...) plus each node's metrics. Trials do NOT land here — the driver silences the tracker during search re-execution on purpose, so a sink records what a run SHIPPED, not what it explored; the per-trial scores live in the search node's record in the run dir and in the run report.

tracking.notes: Excluded from the identity hash — where metrics land says nothing about what the run computes.
